avoid_supplements.name: High-dose Vitamin A
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Both niacin and excess vitamin A can cause hepatotoxicity and skin toxicity; additive risk of liver injury and hypervitaminosis A
avoid_supplements.action: Avoid concurrent high-dose supplementation; monitor liver function tests and vitamin A levels

avoid_supplements.name: Chromium picolinate
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Both agents affect glucose metabolism and may cause hypoglycemia; niacin impairs glucose tolerance while chromium enhances insulin sensitivity
avoid_supplements.action: Use together only under physician supervision with frequent glucose monitoring

caution_supplements.name: Fish Oil (Omega-3)
caution_supplements.mechanism: Additive lipid-lowering effects; both reduce triglycerides and may potentiate anticoagulant effects
caution_supplements.action: Monitor lipid panel and coagulation parameters; educate on bleeding risk

caution_supplements.name: Red Yeast Rice
caution_supplements.mechanism: Contains lovastatin (statin-like); additive lipid-lowering effect and increased risk of myopathy with niacin
caution_supplements.action: Monitor for muscle pain, weakness, or elevated CK; separate dosing by 2+ hours if used together

caution_supplements.name: Milk Thistle (Silymarin)
caution_supplements.mechanism: Both metabolized hepatically; theoretical increased hepatic workload in high-dose niacin therapy
caution_supplements.action: Monitor baseline and periodic liver function tests

avoid_foods.name: Excessive alcohol
avoid_foods.mechanism: Alcohol potentiates niacin-induced flushing, hepatotoxicity, and hyperglycemia; increases vasodilation and adverse effects
avoid_foods.action: Counsel patient to limit or eliminate alcohol; niacin use contraindicated in active liver disease or heavy alcohol use

caution_foods.name: High-sugar/refined carbohydrate foods
caution_foods.mechanism: Niacin impairs glucose tolerance and increases blood glucose; high glycemic foods may exacerbate hyperglycemia risk
caution_foods.action: Recommend low glycemic index foods; monitor fasting glucose and HbA1c in diabetic patients

caution_foods.name: Caffeine-containing beverages
caution_foods.mechanism: Caffeine may increase niacin-induced flushing and vasodilation; mild additive stimulant effect
caution_foods.action: Advise patient to limit caffeine intake; take niacin at night or with food to minimize flushing

monitoring_notes: Monitor liver function tests (ALT, AST, bilirubin) at baseline and periodically, especially at doses >2g/day. Track fasting glucose and HbA1c in diabetic patients, as niacin impairs glucose tolerance; educate on flushing management (take with food, use aspirin pretreatment as directed by physician).
